blocks.text: Reading Order in Two Column Layouts
Abstract: We test whether reading order is recovered for a page with a full width title, a full width abstract and two columns of body text.
Column detection is a classic problem in document analysis. A reader expects the left column to be read before the right one, even when lines in both columns share the same baseline.
We generated pages with two columns of equal width separated by a gutter of twenty points. Headings use a bold face so that a parser can detect them from font information alone.
The parser recovered the order of every block on the page. The right column begins only after the left column has ended, which matches the order intended by the author.
Simple geometric rules are sufficient for clean two column layouts. Complex layouts with floats require further work.
